symbols.name: address bits per record
symbols.meaning: The number of address bits within a record, log base 2 of r.
symbols.quote: Let $\ell=\log_2 r$ be the number of address bits within a record.

symbols.name: number of axes
symbols.quote: The $D=d-1$ axes have lengths $t_i\in\{2^{\ell-1},2^\ell\}$, where $d$ is a size parameter with $d\ell=O(p)$.

symbols.name: size parameter
symbols.meaning: A size parameter one more than the number of axes, with d times ell of order p.
symbols.quote: The $D=d-1$ axes have lengths $t_i\in\{2^{\ell-1},2^\ell\}$, where $d$ is a size parameter with $d\ell=O(p)$.

symbols.name: axis length
symbols.meaning: The length of axis i, either 2^(ell-1) or 2^ell.
symbols.quote: The $D=d-1$ axes have lengths $t_i\in\{2^{\ell-1},2^\ell\}$, where $d$ is a size parameter with $d\ell=O(p)$.

symbols.name: record count
symbols.meaning: The number of polynomial records, the product of the axis lengths.
symbols.quote: $M$, the product of the $t_i$, is the number of records and $T=rM$ the number of complex coefficients.

symbols.name: coefficient count
symbols.meaning: The number of complex coefficients, r times M.
symbols.quote: $M$, the product of the $t_i$, is the number of records and $T=rM$ the number of complex coefficients.

symbols.name: precision
symbols.meaning: The precision in bits: coefficient parts are multiples of 2^-p.
symbols.quote: Coefficients are [fixed-point Gaussian dyadic records](fixed-point.md) with parts multiples of $2^{-p}$, where $p$ is the precision in bits.

symbols.name: chunk width
symbols.meaning: The width in bits of an address chunk.

symbols.name: interchange exponent
symbols.meaning: The fixed exponent below 1 in the cost of chunk interchange.
symbols.quote: The fixed exponents $\tau,\lambda'<1$ are those of chunk interchange and the layer.

symbols.name: layer exponent
symbols.meaning: The fixed exponent below 1 in the cost of the simultaneous layer.
symbols.quote: The fixed exponents $\tau,\lambda'<1$ are those of chunk interchange and the layer.

symbols.name: bit reversal
symbols.meaning: The bit-reversal order in which forward outputs are written.
symbols.quote: Outputs come in bit-reversal order $B$, which the pointwise product keeps.

symbols.name: layout permutation
symbols.meaning: The permutation of records built by the prefix moves and chunk exchanges.
symbols.quote: The layout permutation $L$, built below, adds one record permutation to the [retained frequency order](frequency-order.md): the forward entry with frequency address $j$ is stored at $L(Bj)$.

symbols.name: frequency address
symbols.meaning: A frequency address of an output entry.
symbols.quote: The layout permutation $L$, built below, adds one record permutation to the [retained frequency order](frequency-order.md): the forward entry with frequency address $j$ is stored at $L(Bj)$.

symbols.name: low-bit remainder
symbols.meaning: (ell-1) mod K, the number of low bits per axis beyond whole chunks.
symbols.quote: Call an axis long if it has $\ell$ address bits and short if $\ell-1$; put $b=(\ell-1)\bmod K$ and $q=\lfloor(\ell-1)/K\rfloor$.

symbols.name: chunks per axis
symbols.meaning: The number of whole K-bit chunks in ell-1 bits.
symbols.quote: Call an axis long if it has $\ell$ address bits and short if $\ell-1$; put $b=(\ell-1)\bmod K$ and $q=\lfloor(\ell-1)/K\rfloor$.

symbols.name: round contraction
symbols.meaning: The contraction applied by one round.
symbols.quote: Each round applies a contraction $\mathcal H$ and a signed coefficient permutation $J_E$, then truncates with $Q_p$ toward zero.

symbols.name: signed permutation
symbols.meaning: The signed coefficient permutation applied in a round.
symbols.quote: Each round applies a contraction $\mathcal H$ and a signed coefficient permutation $J_E$, then truncates with $Q_p$ toward zero.

symbols.name: truncation
symbols.meaning: Truncation toward zero of real and imaginary parts to the 2^-p grid.
symbols.quote: Each round applies a contraction $\mathcal H$ and a signed coefficient permutation $J_E$, then truncates with $Q_p$ toward zero.

relations.quote: The tape layout rearranges the address bits of a [synthetic polynomial transform](synthetic-transform.md) and turns each round into one [simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-layer.md).
The tape layout rearranges the address bits of a [synthetic polynomial transform](synthetic-transform.md) and turns each round into one [simultaneous butterfly layer](simultaneous-layer.md).
Scanning target positions left to right, the layout exchanges chunks by the [fast address-chunk interchange](address-interchange.md), each costing $O(TpK^\tau)$, to group equal-index chunks.
The layout permutation $L$, built below, adds one record permutation to the [retained frequency order](frequency-order.md): the forward entry with frequency address $j$ is stored at $L(Bj)$.

derivations.quote: Adding the costs, both procedures cost $O(Tp[dK+pK^{\tau-1}+\ell d^{\lambda'}])$ with error below $\sqrt2\,\ell\,2^{-p}$.
